confirmed.title: 79 named observations (including all of E1/E2) can never PASS because case profiles omit profiles that the oracle's requiredLayers demand
confirmed.failure_scenario: Every E1 oracle has requiredLayers API/DB/MCP, so the assembler requires the profiles {scenarios, mcp}. E1/case.json declares profiles ['scenarios'], so links are only ever created for 'scenarios' (lines 209/221). For 'mcp', clause_states is empty and the observation stays NOT_RUN no matter what runs. Plan §11 says S4 must close by passing E1. A correct S4 system can therefore never have E1 accepted by the coverage verifier, while `./verify prepare` reports PREPARED. That pushes teams to close E1 through separate actual-s4 receipts, or to edit the catalog/lock to drop MCP.
confirmed.evidence: I ran Assembly.catalog()+declarations() read-only at HEAD. It found 79 observations with a required profile that has zero assertion links: E1 20 and E2 15 (mcp), T09 13, T12 4 and T04 3 (contracts), T25 7 (mcp, skills), V8 6 and T23 5 (scenarios), T15 3 (regulatory), C3 3 (skills). It reported preparation_problems=[]. CatalogLinkValidator.java:28-29 only checks that a link exists and, for quantities, the fixed value; it ignores requiredLayers. The coverage README requires each requiredLayers path to have executed assertions.
confirmed.fix: In both CatalogLinkValidator and the assembler preparation, require at least one linked assertion for each LAYER_PROFILE(requiredLayers) value, from a case that declares that profile. Then add real assertions and profiles to the cases (E1/E2 MCP path, T15 regulatory evidence, T04/T09/T12 contracts, T23/V8 scenarios, T25 and C3 skills/mcp), or change the catalog through the reviewed lock procedure. Reconcile E1's MCP requirement with plan §11, where E1 belongs to S4 and MCP to S5.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute the defect. I reproduced it read-only at HEAD 7b540e8f, which is past Step 2 and includes the S4 integrations. The overstated parts are the S4 framing and the line the claim points at.

What I confirmed:
- **Required profiles.** `verification/coverage/assemble.py:151` builds `requiredProfiles` from `LAYER_PROFILE` over the oracle's `requiredLayers`.
- **Link creation.** Lines 209 and 221 create declarations and assertion links only for `effective_profiles(case.profiles)`.
- **Status rule.** Lines 684-686 set a required profile with no links to NOT_RUN, so the observation stays NOT_RUN.
- **Reproduction.** I ran `Assembly.catalog()` and `declarations()` in Python. It returned `preparation_problems=[]`, and exactly 79 observations have a required profile with zero links:

  | Case | Missing profile | Observations |
  |---|---|---|
  | E1 | mcp | 20 |
  | E2 | mcp | 15 |
  | T09 | contracts | 13 |
  | T25 | mcp | 7 |
  | V8 | scenarios | 6 |
  | T23 | scenarios | 5 |
  | T12 | contracts | 4 |
  | T04 | contracts | 3 |
  | T15 | regulatory | 3 |
  | C3 | skills | 3 |

- **E1/E2.** Their `case.json` files declare only `['scenarios']`, while every E1/E2 oracle requires API, DB and MCP.
- **Java validator.** `CatalogLinkValidator.java` lines 17-39 checks only that each observation has a link and that quantities are fixed. It never reads `requiredLayers` or case profiles, so `./verify prepare` gets no warning either.
- **No other evidence route.** Nothing in `mcp-tests` or `skills-tests` references E1/E2 oracles, and the assembler links evidence only through `case.json` assertions.
- **Not previously found.** No prior review (`step-2-review.md`, `step-2-common-review.md`) or status document (`task-status.md`, step-3 and s4 notes) records this gap.
- **README contradiction.** `verification/coverage/README.md` says a set with one clause missing is not prepared, and that observation `requiredLayers` must each link to their required profile. Here preparation completes with whole required layers missing.

Mitigations and overstatements:
1. **Fail-closed.** The observation and the overall gate stay NOT_RUN, so no wrong system can PASS and no NOT_RUN is hidden as PASS. That keeps it out of P0.
2. **Line attribution.** `assemble.py:685` behaves as the README specifies. The defects are the case profile and assertion declarations plus the missing preparation-time check in the Java validator and the assembler.
3. **S4 framing.** The whole-coverage assembler is not the S4 gate, and it cannot PASS at S4 anyway because the model and BTP profiles are pending. The lasting effect is that the S6 rule "required D/C/V/E traceability all PASS" can never be met without reworking the cases or the mapping.
4. **Mapping, not just cases.** Part of the gap may come from the mapping rather than the cases. `LAYER_PROFILE` maps API/DB only to `scenarios` and UNIT only to `contracts`, so V8 and T23 work run under recovery or deployment, and the T04/T09/T12 UNIT clauses, can never satisfy the requirement. The fix could be a mapping change or added profiles.

Severity: it still qualifies as P1, because plan and catalog obligations have no assertions in the Step 2 test suite while preparation reports them complete. These include E1/E2 through MCP, T15 regulatory review, C3 and T25 skills/MCP, and V8/T23 API/DB.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute the claim. I checked it against the code and ran the assembler's own declaration step, read-only.

1. **The mapping works as claimed.** In verification/coverage/assemble.py:
   - Lines 25-26 map each requiredLayer to a profile (LAYER_PROFILE).
   - Line 151 computes requiredProfiles from the oracle's requiredLayers.
   - Lines 216-219 attach assertionLinks only for profiles the case itself declares (effective_profiles(case.profiles)).
   - Lines 221-223 raise a preparation problem only when an observation has zero links.
   - Lines 683-687 set a required profile's state to NOT_RUN when no link exists on that profile.

2. **The script confirms it.** I instantiated Assembly and ran catalog() and declarations() on the current branch head (7b540e8f). The result was 0 preparation problems, yet 79 named observations in 21 oracles have a required profile with no link on it:

   | Missing profile | Observations |
   |---|---|
   | mcp | 42 |
   | contracts | 20 |
   | scenarios | 11 |
   | skills | 6 |
   | regulatory | 3 |

   The per-oracle list matches the claim exactly (T04, T09x3, T12, T15, T23x2, T25x3, C3, V8x3, E1x3, E2x3).

3. **Nothing upstream catches it.**
   - The `./verify prepare` path doesn't check this. Main.prepare and CatalogLinkValidator only check that each observation has at least one assertion, that the oracle belongs to the right case, that quantity assertions are fixed, and that source hashes match. Neither looks at requiredLayers. A grep finds requiredLayers only in the catalog, its schema, the READMEs, assemble.py:151, and one catalog mutation test.
   - Main.java:43 runs a case under a profile only when the case lists that profile. So E1/E2 never run under mcp, and T04/T09/T12 never run under contracts.
   - test_coverage.py has no test for required-profile coverage.
   - The step-2 reviews never mention it.

4. **PREPARED is reachable and was reported.** Lines 637-650 give PREPARED when there are no preparation problems, the fresh `./verify prepare` reports PREPARED, and model preparation is PREPARED. step-2-review.md and task-status.md record Step 2 closing with "preparation PREPARED, coverage 문제0·VALID". That contradicts coverage/README.md, which says a missing clause means preparation is not complete ("조항 하나를 빠뜨리면 준비 완료가 아니다") and that each requiredLayer is linked to its profile.

5. **The T15 regulatory gap is worse than claimed.** contracts/acceptance-case.schema.json limits profiles to schema, contracts, scenarios, recovery, mcp, skills, model and deployment. 'regulatory' is not allowed. So no schema-valid case can ever link T15.unresolved-real-policy's REGULATORY_REVIEW observations. Meanwhile assemble.py lists 'regulatory' in PROFILES and requires that profile to PASS. Fixing this needs a schema change, not just case data.

**Where the claim is overstated:**
- This is fail-closed. No observation, and so no overall result, can become PASS, which means a wrong system cannot pass. That is why it is not P0.
- The aside about plan D20 "two entry points" and E1 is off: E1's requirementIds are D05/D09/D13/D15/D16/D17/D18/D19, not D20, and plan §13.3 does not name MCP for E1. MCP for E1/E2 comes from the independent catalog's requiredLayers.
- The cited line numbers are a few lines off (the links are at about 216-219, not 221).

**Why P1 stands:** The catalog requires these layers, but no case or profile path in the repo executes them. For regulatory, the case schema forbids such a path outright. The step-2 tests therefore do not cover those required observations, while the preparation signal used to close Step 2 reports complete. Later Steps will hit a coverage gate that can never close, which invites weakening the catalog instead of adding real assertions.

**Fix:** The claim's fix holds, with one addition. In declarations(), record a preparationProblem whenever a requiredProfile has no assertionLink, and add 'regulatory' to the acceptance-case schema enum, or else define a separate regulatory evidence-binding path for T15.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute the claim. I checked every part of it against HEAD of /Volumes/VideoStore/Developer/mulino-coreano-ontology, and against d7ef715, the commit where Step 2 was declared COMPLETE.

**1. The catalog requires MCP for every E1 and E2 oracle.**
- In `verification/requirements/mandatory-oracles.json`, the six E1/E2 oracles all have `requiredLayers` ['API','DB','MCP'].
- They hold 20 E1 observations (11+7+2) and 15 E2 observations (5+6+4).
- V8.fresh-install, V8.ontology-upgrade-preservation and V8.db-blob-definition-restore require API and DB. Those layers map to the 'scenarios' profile, and these oracles have 6 observations between them.

**2. The cases do not declare those profiles, and this is unchanged since Step 2.**
- `verification/cases/E1/case.json` and `E2/case.json` declare profiles ['scenarios'] only. Their routes are api×93 (E1) and api×43 (E2), with no mcp or wire route.
- V8 declares schema, contracts, recovery, mcp and deployment, but not scenarios.
- `git diff d7ef715 HEAD` shows no change to these case files, to `assemble.py`, or to the catalog.

**3. A missing profile can never become PASS.**
- In `assemble.py:240-246`, a link's profile comes only from the profiles its own case declares.
- At `assemble.py:684-686`, a required profile with no linked assertion is marked NOT_RUN, and so is the observation.
- The Java harness gives no other route. `Main.java:43` skips any case that does not declare the profile being run, so `./verify mcp` never runs E1 or E2.

**4. Nothing else catches the gap.**
- The preparation check at `assemble.py:224-226` reports an observation only when it has zero links.
- `CatalogLinkValidator.java` checks linkage and fixed-quantity assertions only; it never looks at layers or profiles.
- `PreparationValidator`, `validate.py` and `test_coverage.py` contain no check of required profiles against linked profiles.
- Running `Assembly.catalog()` and `declarations()` read-only at HEAD gives 0 preparation problems.
- The same run finds 79 observations with a required profile that no assertion covers: C3 skills 3, E1 mcp 20, E2 mcp 15, T04 contracts 3, T09 contracts 13, T12 contracts 4, T15 regulatory 3, T23 scenarios 5, T25 mcp 7 and skills 3, V8 scenarios 6. This matches the claim.
- `step-2-review.md:128,147` records 'coverage VALID' with an empty problem list, and Step 2 was declared COMPLETE.

**5. This contradicts the repo's own contract.**
- The coverage README (lines 94 and 114-115) says preparation is not complete if even one clause is missing.
- It also says each observation's `requiredLayers` must be tied to an executed assertion for each required profile.
- Plan §3.4 requires the two entry points (noun and verb reads) to return the same results.
- Plan §11 S6 requires all D/C/V/E traceability to PASS.

**Why it stays P1 rather than P0.** The gap fails closed: these observations end as NOT_RUN, never as a false PASS. So a wrong system cannot pass acceptance. But a catalog-mandated layer (MCP for E1/E2) has no test at all, and preparation reports itself complete. The gap would only show up at final S6 assembly, as permanent NOT_RUN that the cases cannot fix.

**Fix.** The claim's fix is correct:
- Add MCP-route actions and assertions to E1 and E2 that read the same snapshot over MCP.
- Add the 'scenarios' profile to V8, and close the other listed profile gaps.
- Make preparation, in both `assemble.py` and `CatalogLinkValidator`, raise a problem for every (observation, requiredProfile) pair that has no linked assertion in a case declaring that profile.

confirmed.title: An empty or null normative lock turns off lock enforcement in the coverage assembler
confirmed.failure_scenario: Overwrite verification/requirements/normative-contract-lock.json with `{}` (or `null`/`[]`/`0`). Then weaken a locked oracle without changing any counts, e.g. E1.full-flow-quantities/warehouse-current-held from 80 to 100, and change the E1 case assertion to match. `./verify prepare` still reports PREPARED because Java Main.prepare/CatalogLinkValidator never read the lock. Assembly.catalog() records zero preparation problems. A system whose W on-hand is 100 instead of the plan's 80 can therefore reach coverage PASS.
confirmed.evidence: assemble.py:124-125 reads the lock and calls validate_catalog.validate only inside `if lock:`. read() returns parsed JSON that evaluates false and records no issue. I reproduced this in a /tmp copy (the repo was not modified): with lock `{}` and with lock `null`, after weakening E1 80->100, preparation_problems=[] and problems=[]. The same edit with the real lock fails with 'E1.full-flow-quantities: fixed contract changed or weakened'. The CLI validate_catalog.py does reject an empty lock (KeyError gives INVALID), but nothing runs it automatically: there is no CI, no Java test and no ./verify step that calls it. test_coverage.py has no empty-lock test. README lines 96-99 treat a coordinated catalog+lock re-hash as the only bypass; blanking the lock needs no re-hashing.
confirmed.fix: Treat any lock value that is not a dict with sourceFiles/oracleContracts as FAIL, and always call validator.validate(catalog, lock, root) when the file exists. Run the same lock check from Java prepare/coverage (or have them invoke validate_catalog.py). Add assembler tests for `{}`, `null`, `[]` and `0`. Record the lock hash somewhere outside the lock file, e.g. in a reviewed T25 fixture or in reviewUpdates together with an approval reference.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute the mechanism. The failure path is real and reachable, but P1 overstates its impact.

What I confirmed by reading the code:
- verification/coverage/assemble.py:124-137. `read()` returns whatever JSON the file contains and records no issue when the content parses. The independent validator only runs inside `if lock:`. So a lock of `{}`, `null`, `[]` or `0` skips `validate_catalog.validate()` and records nothing. A missing lock file gives NOT_RUN, so the fail-open behaviour applies only to falsy content.
- I reproduced it outside the repo. I copied the catalog, lock, validator, schema and source files into /tmp and set E1.full-flow-quantities/warehouse-current-held from 80 to 100:
  - With the real lock, `Assembly.catalog()` returns the FAIL "fixed contract changed or weakened".
  - With a lock of `{}`, `None`, `[]` or `0` it returns 122 oracles, 499 observations and `preparation_problems=[]`.
- Nothing else in the gate catches the weakened catalog value:
  - `catalog()` checks only case IDs, counts and catalog.sourceFiles hashes, which cover the normative docs and not the oracle contents.
  - `run_case` compares the runtime assertion's expected value to the case file's declared value, not to the catalog's.
  - Java `Main.prepare`/`CatalogLinkValidator` (CatalogLinkValidator.java:53-56) compare the case's decimal expected value to the catalog's expected value. This forces the attacker to edit both files consistently, but the Java code never reads the lock.
  - `./verify` never calls validate_catalog.py, and there is no CI workflow.
  - The only other copy of the lock hash is in verification/coverage/checks/not-run-summary.json, a saved output that nothing compares against.
  - test_coverage.py has no test for an empty or null lock.
- `validate_catalog.validate()` itself would reject `{}` with a KeyError, because of `lock or json.loads(...)`. The gap is purely the assembler's `if lock:` guard.

Why I lower it to P2:
1. The exploit is not "a wrong system passes". Someone has to deliberately edit three verification artifacts: the catalog, the case assertion and the lock. verification/requirements/README.md:94-99 already says that changing the catalog and lock together bypasses the fence; the lock is a reviewed drift fence, not an authority.
2. Re-hashing a single contract is trivial: `contractSha256 = digest(oracle)`, one line using the validator's own function. So blanking the lock gives an attacker no new capability. It also produces a far more conspicuous diff (about 42 KB deleted) than updating one hash.
3. The remaining harm is a fail-closed violation. If the lock is accidentally corrupted or truncated to a falsy JSON value, for example by a botched regeneration, oracle-contract enforcement turns off silently with no NOT_RUN or FAIL signal. A missing file is reported. That is a real weak-guard defect, but it does not show an uncovered plan requirement.

Fix, still valid:
- When the lock file exists, always call `validator.validate(catalog, lock, root)`. Treat any lock that is not a dict containing sourceFiles and oracleContracts as FAIL.
- Add assembler tests for `{}`, `null`, `[]` and `0`.
- Optionally run the lock check from `./verify prepare` too.

confirmed.title: Model-corpus oracles can be weakened without detection: generate.py rewrites every hash and no check runs the corpus validator
confirmed.failure_scenario: Change M16 turn-1 `response.onHand.value` from '80' to '100'. This contradicts §13.3 E1, where W currently holds 80. Rerun generate.py: registry, bindings and semantic-paths all get the new corpus SHA. model-corpus/validate.py still prints VALID because M16 is not in MANDATORY_ASSERTIONS. The Java model-binding prepare and assemble.py only compare hashes against each other, so the weakened E1 query oracle (×3 repeats) is accepted. The same applies to any count-preserving edit of expected values, maxNew or obligations in the roughly 45 cases that MANDATORY_ASSERTIONS does not cover.
confirmed.evidence: I reproduced this in a /tmp copy: after the edit and a generate.py run, validate.py printed corpusIntegrity VALID, Assembly.model_bindings(...) returned preparation_problems=[], and the corpus SHA equalled the registry SHA. The only drift checks are hash consistency: BindingContract.java:20-22 and 78, and assemble.py:542 and 559. generate.py computes H from corpus.json and writes it into registry.json, semantic-paths.json and every binding.json. Nothing in verify, model-binding/run, assemble.py or harness/src/main references model-corpus/validate.py. Unlike the T/C/V/E catalog, there is no normative lock for the corpus.
confirmed.fix: Add a reviewed model-corpus lock with per-turn digests of oracle assertions, allowedEffects/forbiddenEffects, obligations, uatCompletion and sitDirectCommand, plus the corpus SHA. Make model-binding prepare and assemble.py run model-corpus/validate.py and the lock check. Pin the corpus SHA in the locked T25.model-corpus-and-budget fixture. Make generate.py refuse to regenerate when the corpus SHA differs from the locked SHA.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute the mechanism. It is real and reachable, but I rate it P2 rather than P1.

What I confirmed:
- generate.py:12 sets H to the sha256 of whatever corpus.json is on disk. It writes H into semantic-paths.json (l.42), every cases/*/binding.json (l.71) and registry.json (l.77).
- BindingContract.java:20-22 and :45 only check that the registry, path-map and binding hashes agree with each other ("Closed corpus hash drift").
- assemble.py:541 and :558 compare the report, path-map and registry hashes against the current corpus descriptor. That is only a consistency check.
- registry.baselineCommit (feaca0af…) is copied into the report (BindingContract.java:105). Nothing compares the corpus bytes to that commit.
- The T25.model-corpus-and-budget lock entry (normative-contract-lock.json:905) and its catalog fixture pin only counts (60, 20/10/10/10/10, x3, ≥10 foreign). They do not pin content.
- No harness test, verify mode, model-binding/run or assemble.py invokes model-corpus/validate.py.
- The current SHA 570ce461… appears only in regenerable or evidence files (model-binding/*, model-corpus/checks/evidence.json, coverage/checks). None of them is read as a lock.
- MANDATORY_ASSERTIONS (validate.py:29-60) pins only 14 cases. M16 is not among them.

Reproduction in /tmp/corpuslock.5BNM (a copy of model-corpus and model-binding only):
- I set M16 response.onHand.value from "80" to "100". validate.py printed VALID. generate.py rewrote registry.corpusSha256 to equal the new corpus SHA.
- I also made two model-behaviour weakenings: M08 ALLOCATION maxNew 1→2, and M03 effects.receiptCount changed from eq 1 to lte 2 with QUANTITY/RECEIPT maxNew 2. validate.py still printed VALID, and all 61 corpus self-tests passed.
- I did not run the Java prepare step (no builds allowed). Code reading shows it would only find the hashes consistent.

Why P2, not P1:
1. The cited M16/E1 example is the weakest case. Changing the oracle to 100 makes a correct server, which reports 80 from the seeded e1.onHand=80, FAIL. A server that wrongly reports 100 would still be caught by the separately locked deterministic E1/T09/C2 catalog oracles. That edit therefore does not let a wrong system through overall acceptance.
2. The real exposure is the oracles that only the corpus holds: maxNew bounds, allowed/forbidden effect classes, obligations and operators on unpinned cases. Loosening them lets a model or agent that duplicates or over-executes effects pass the S5 model gate. That is a weak-oracle and tamper-protection gap.
3. Exploiting it needs a committed corpus edit plus regeneration. That shows up in the diff across 60+ binding files, and the plan §13.3 and AGENTS.md ("oracle을 줄여 PASS를 만들지 않는다") already forbid it. The gap is a missing mechanical lock, unlike the T/C/V/E catalog, not an uncovered plan requirement.
4. The model gate is NOT_RUN and R8 is unauthorized, so no current verdict is affected.

Misleading guidance that makes this worth fixing:
- Code calls the corpus an "immutable source oracle" or "Closed corpus" (BindingContract.java:10/21, assemble.py:443/542), but nothing holds it to a reviewed value.
- The model-corpus README "필수 반례" table lists M16, M17, M23, M28, M42, M44, M48, M49, M58, M14, M18 and M60 as mandatory counterexamples, but the validator does not pin them.

Fix:
- Make generate.py fail unless the corpus SHA, or per-turn digests of assertions, allowed/forbidden effects, obligations, sitDirectCommand and uatCompletion, match a reviewed lock entry. One option is to add the corpus SHA to the T25 normative lock; another is to check it against git show registry.baselineCommit:corpus.json.
- Enforce the same check in BindingContract.prepare and assemble.py.
- Running validate.py in the pipeline alone would not catch this, because M16, M08 and M03 are not in MANDATORY_ASSERTIONS. The lock is the necessary part.

confirmed.title: Coverage can report PASS from a dirty working tree, so the recorded code commit does not identify the tested code
confirmed.failure_scenario: Run the actual profiles with uncommitted backend changes, e.g. a fixture-specific shortcut. Receipts record codeCommit=HEAD, which equals the assembly commit. The assembler computes complete=True and writes gateComplete:true together with workingTreeDirty:true, and validate.py later accepts the saved manifest. §13.4 requires evidence to name the exact code commit.
confirmed.evidence: workingTreeDirty is only recorded (lines 77 and 701). `complete` (line 694), validate_manifest (lines 711-728) and the PASS branch of runtime-manifest.schema.json never reference it. execution-receipt.schema.json has no dirty or tree-hash field.
confirmed.fix: Require workingTreeDirty == false for PASS in assemble/validate_manifest and in the schema. Record git status or a tree hash in every actual receipt and reject dirty runs.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute the claim. I checked it against branch feat/ontology-implementation at 7b540e8f.

What the code does:
- verification/coverage/assemble.py:77 computes working_tree_dirty from `git status --porcelain`. When a commit is passed in, it is forced to True.
- The flag is only written to the output, at line 701.
- The gate at line 694 is `complete = runtime == 'PASS' and preparation == 'PREPARED' and not self.preparation_problems`. It does not read the flag.
- validate_manifest (lines 711-735) never checks workingTreeDirty.
- validate_saved re-creates Assembly(root) and compares only codeCommit to HEAD. Its list of compared keys leaves out workingTreeDirty.
- In runtime-manifest.schema.json the property is a plain boolean (line 236). The `status == PASS` branch of the allOf (lines 692-737) does not require it to be false.
- execution-receipt.schema.json has additionalProperties:false and only the fields schemaVersion, evidenceClass, codeCommit, executionIdentity, command, versions, reportArtifact, inputs, artifacts and environment. A receipt therefore cannot record a dirty state or a tree hash.
- receipt() (lines 268-270) only checks `receipt.codeCommit == self.commit`, which is HEAD.
- The `--check-preparation` path checks that prepare.json's codeCommit matches but ignores its workingTreeDirty, even though the Java harness's base() writes that field (Main.java:100).
- Backend and product source files are never hashed into inputArtifacts. Uncommitted product edits therefore leave no trace except the ungated dirty flag.

Things that might have neutralized it, and why they don't:
1. The later S1-S4 actual runners (verification/actual/s4/build.py:8 and receipt.py:36) do refuse dirty source. However, they emit S4_DISPOSABLE_RUN_RECEIPT records. The coverage assembler never reads those, and nothing converts them into coverage-format receipts. A git grep for `reportArtifact` producers finds only the coverage files themselves, and runtime-evidence-index.json is empty. The final §13.4 gate is the assembler, and it takes any well-formed receipt.
2. A clean-tree requirement is workable. Evidence lives under the gitignored verification/harness/target/ (git check-ignore confirms this, and it matches the README example paths), and the assembler writes its own transcript there too. Committing evidence would change HEAD and break the codeCommit match anyway. So nothing forces evidence to dirty the tree, and the gap is not intentional.
3. No prior review covers this: there is no dirty or clean-tree item in step-1-review.md, step-2-review.md or step-2-common-review.md.
4. test_coverage.py builds every case with Assembly(root, COMMIT), which forces dirty=True, and still expects PASS on the model and run_case paths. Nothing tests the case where a dirty tree must fail.

The scenario is reachable. Run the actual profiles with uncommitted product edits, and have the receipts record HEAD as the runner sees it. All other conditions met, the manifest comes out as status PASS, exit 0, gateComplete/runtimeComplete/productRuntimeClaimed true, and workingTreeDirty true. validate.py then accepts it, because the tree is still dirty and HEAD is unchanged. That contradicts §13.4, which requires the manifest to identify the code commit that was tested.

Why the severity stays at P2 rather than P0 or P1:
- The dirty flag is recorded honestly, so a human reading the manifest can spot it.
- No coverage-receipt producer exists yet.
- The S-step runners already enforce clean source on their own path.
- The harm is wrong attribution, not a forged business result.

Fix:
- Make `complete` in assemble() require `not self.working_tree_dirty`.
- Reject `status == PASS` with workingTreeDirty true in validate_manifest, and add `workingTreeDirty: {const: false}` to the schema's PASS branch.
- Have validate_saved recompute the dirty state and compare it.
- Add sourceClean (or the porcelain status) and a tree hash to execution-receipt.schema.json, require them to be clean in receipt(), and apply the same check to prepare.json.workingTreeDirty in --check-preparation.

confirmed.title: UAT QUERY turns pass without the model actually answering, because the harness's own context read satisfies the response oracles
confirmed.failure_scenario: For M01 and M16 (the E1 quantities), the harness calls getObject ACTOR_PERMITTED_BUSINESS_CONTEXT before the agent runs. In UAT that read is added to the captured calls, and transcript.apiAssertionSources may map every response.* path to it (checkAssertion permits getObject for QUERY). The model replies '조회했습니다' with no numbers. The extractor reports execution=READ with empty claims.assertions, FinalResponseObservation only checks claims that are present, and finalOnly skips the outcome check. The turn PASSes with full credit although the question was never answered. A wrong numeric answer would only be caught if it were extracted as a claim.
confirmed.evidence: ModelBindingRunner.java:161 adds the context authenticatedRead to captured calls. Line 205 allows `call.capabilityId().equals("getObject")` for QUERY. Line 116 sets finalOnly for UAT QUERY. FinalResponseObservation.java:35-43 iterate only over the claims present. model-binding README:169 explicitly allows the context read as the API source.
confirmed.fix: For READ outcomes, require the final-response observation to cover every oracle response.* path (value and unit), verified against authenticated API data, or otherwise require the answer content to be present. Do not let the pre-agent harness read be the only evidence for the model's answer.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this. I traced a UAT QUERY turn through the evaluate() code in /Volumes/VideoStore/Developer/mulino-coreano-ontology/verification/harness/src/main/java/org/mulino/verification/modelbinding/ModelBindingRunner.java, and the turn can pass without the model's answer content ever being checked.

How such a turn passes:
- **Context read counts as an API source.** Line 161 adds the pre-agent context read to the captured calls. That read is the harness's own `getObject` call with view `ACTOR_PERMITTED_BUSINESS_CONTEXT`, made by `read-probe-actor` (lines 49-50). In CapturedApiObservation, `response(path)` returns whichever call `apiAssertionSources` maps the path to. In `checkAssertion` (line 205), `capabilityId == getObject` is accepted for any QUERY. So every `response.*` oracle assertion (all mapped as `AUTHENTICATED_API` in semantic-paths.json) can be satisfied entirely by server data.
- **No tool call is required for QUERY.** `requireExecutionCall` returns early for QUERY (CapturedApiObservation line 60).
- **No outcome check for UAT QUERY.** Line 116 sets `finalOnly` for UAT QUERY, and line 118 then skips the outcome check.
- **Only extracted claims are checked.** `FinalResponseObservation.check` (lines 34-43) requires execution claim `READ` and an outcome that is blank or `READ`. It then iterates only the assertions the extractor reported. An empty assertions array checks nothing. An empty `residualObligations` list also passes `evaluator.obligations`, because the list of needed obligations is empty.
- **Clarification check passes on a missing field.** Line 126 only compares `clarification.required` (missing = false), which matches the oracle.

The result: for M01, the answer "조회했습니다" with no numbers reaches report status PASS. The same holds for M16, which asks for the remaining QC/return/settlement owners; omitting them passes.

The gap is wider than the claim says. The extractor schema (final-response-observation.schema.json) and line 19 fix coverage at exactly CLAIMED_EFFECTS, COMPLETION and RESIDUAL_RESPONSIBILITY. No category covers values reported from a read. A fully compliant extractor therefore has no duty to extract a wrong number such as "팔 수 있는 양 100". M01's focus, telling consignment stock apart from customer custody, is then never tested on the model side.

The README confirms this is the design rather than something another check covers:
- model-binding README line 169 explicitly allows the context read as the API source.
- The final-response section says only "언급한" (mentioned) quantities and owners are compared.

No test in ModelBindingResponseEvidenceTest covers a QUERY answer with no content. Prior Step 2 findings S8 and S9 cover only false completion at preflight and replay wiring; neither addresses this gap.

Scope: 22 non-NEEDS_INPUT QUERY turns in the corpus are affected: M01, M05, M06, M15, M16, M17, M20, the second turns of M23/M28/M29, M31-M41 and M43.

Why the severity stays at P2 rather than P1:
- The plan's §13.3 model acceptance metric is "올바른 구조화≥95%, 부당 실행0, 무권한·중복·허위완료0". Structuring is still checked separately by `checkStructuredIntent` (line 105).
- So this weakens the oracle rather than contradicting a stated requirement. It still conflicts with model-corpus README "oracle는 최종 response…를 판정" and the plan's §9.2 "올바른 실제 tool 호출·남은 의무 확인".

Minor inaccuracy in the claim: M01 is tied to T05/C1, not E1; only M16 is the E1 case. This does not affect validity.

The proposed fix is sound: for READ outcomes, require the extractor to report every oracle `response.*` path with its value and unit, verified against the authenticated API data. Also add a coverage category for answered read values so that a missing or incorrect answer fails.

confirmed.title: The §13.3 'clear requests structured correctly ≥95%' threshold is mis-encoded: exact-match hard FAIL in the runner, narrowed denominator in the docs, and no producer of the rate
confirmed.failure_scenario: (a) checkStructuredIntent requires exact equality of status, intentKind, definitionVersion, the missingSlots array order, and USER provenance/sourceRef/sourceText. A correct model that quotes '팔 수 있는 양' instead of the corpus author's excerpt '팔 수' (M01 action slot) throws IllegalArgumentException, the turn becomes FAIL, and the whole model gate FAILs. The plan's 95% rate becomes 100% exact-string matching, which invites later weakening. (b) The model-corpus README (lines 215-217) sets the denominator to only 'clear 20 cases × 3' (M01–M20). The plan contrasts clear requests with ambiguous inputs, so clear but risky requests in M31–M60 drop out of the metric. (c) Nothing in the repo computes clearStructuredIntentRate; only the T25 case expects an extractor to supply it.
confirmed.evidence: ModelBindingRunner.java:200-203 compares each key with equals and requires sourceText equality. The corpus observationContract.slotScope defines sourceText only as 'a verbatim excerpt … supporting normalized meaning' and slots as minimum expectations. grep finds clearStructured only in the corpus/catalog/T25 case data, with no computation.
confirmed.fix: Record a per-turn intent-match metric: sourceText must be a verbatim substring that supports the value, and missingSlots is compared as a set. Aggregate the rate over all non-ambiguous turns and gate on ≥0.95, while keeping the zero-tolerance safety invariants (no improper execution, unauthorized, duplicate or false-completion effects) as hard FAILs. Correct the README denominator.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute the core claim (a). I confirmed it by reading the code; parts (b) and (c) are weaker.

**(a) Confirmed and reachable.**
- In `verification/harness/src/main/java/org/mulino/verification/modelbinding/ModelBindingRunner.java` (lines 200-204), `checkStructuredIntent` uses `JsonNode.equals` to compare four keys: `status`, `intentKind`, `definitionVersion` and `missingSlots`. Jackson's `ArrayNode` equality depends on order. For every expected slot that carries `provenance`, `sourceRef` or `sourceText`, the method also requires exact equality.
- The UAT path calls this method at line 105, inside `evaluate()`. If it throws, the catch at line 133 marks the turn FAIL. `status()` then returns FAIL.
- `ModelBindingGlue.judge` (`verification/harness/src/test/java/org/mulino/verification/modelbinding/ModelBindingGlue.java`, line 15) then fails the Gherkin scenario.

The failing inputs exist in the corpus:
- M01's `action` slot has expected `sourceText` "팔 수" for the utterance "...팔 수 있는 양...". A model that quotes "팔 수 있는 양" fails.
- M03's `evidenceRefs` `sourceText` is the entire utterance.
- M25, M26, M27 and M28 have two-element `missingSlots`, such as `['dueAt','dueInclusive']`. A model that returns the same set in a different order fails.

The runner's exact match contradicts the corpus's own contract in three places:
- `verification/model-corpus/validate.py` (lines 383-384) only requires `sourceText` to be a verbatim substring of the raw turn (`value['sourceText'] in raw`).
- `corpus.json` `observationContract.slotScope` calls slots "minimum semantic expectations" and `sourceText` "a verbatim excerpt ... supporting normalized meaning".
- `verification/model-corpus/README.md` says the oracle does not fix the model's exact sentences.

Nothing neutralizes this. No schema defines `transcript.structuredIntent`, no test exercises `checkStructuredIntent`, and no recorded decision in `docs/` or `.agents/` justifies exact matching. The prior Step 2 reviews do not mention it.

The effect is that the plan's proposed ≥95% structuring rate (plan §13, line 458) becomes 100% exact string and order matching for each case.

**Severity stays P2, not higher.** The defect fails closed: it produces false FAILs for correct models, but it cannot let a wrong system pass. The threshold itself is still only a proposal pending R8.

**(b) Interpretive, not a clear defect.** The plan does not define the denominator for "명확한 요청". The README chose the `clear_synonyms` category (M01-M20, 20 cases × 3) and says so explicitly. The objection still has some basis: another 42 STRUCTURED turns sit in other categories (9 in `ambiguity_target_conflict`, 10 in `query_write_boundary`, 11 in `version_authority_document`, 12 in `business_exception_responsibility`). These are arguably "clear requests" as well.

**(c) Mostly expected at Step 2.** No host extractor exists yet; the README states that UAT PASS is impossible until a real extractor exists. T25 reads the rate from that future extractor. The narrower real gap is in the runner's per-turn reports:
- They record only `status` and `reason`, with no separate intent-match result.
- `checkStructuredIntent` throws before the effect whitelist and other safety checks run.

So a future rate aggregator could not tell an intent miss from a safety failure. If it tolerated 5% FAIL turns, a turn with both a wrong intent and an unauthorized effect would be counted only as an intent miss. That scenario is not reachable today, because every FAIL is a hard FAIL.

**Adjacent issue, not part of this claim.** `ModelBindingGlue.judge` (line 15) labels any non-PASS status, including a real FAIL, as "NOT_IMPLEMENTED ... runtime NOT_RUN". That misreports a real FAIL as NOT_RUN.

**Fix.**
1. Compare `missingSlots` as a set.
2. Accept any USER `sourceText` that is a verbatim substring of the referenced turn and supports the normalized value.
3. Keep exact equality for `value`, `provenance` and `sourceRef`.
4. Record a separate per-turn intent-match flag, and still evaluate the safety invariants after an intent mismatch, so the ≥95% rate and the zero-tolerance counts can be computed independently.
5. Make the README state the denominator as a decision pending R8.

confirmed.title: The assembler accepts the runner's PASS without re-checking observed values against expected, and never compares op or filters
confirmed.failure_scenario: A regression in AssertionEngine/CaseRunner (in the same repo, changeable by implementers) marks `decimalEquals "80"` PASS while the captured e1-db rawRows actually sum to 100, or applies a different op/where/field. The assembler copies the reported status, stores the observed bytes, and the observation becomes PASS. Its evidence integrity checks (hash, identity, profileResult equality) all pass because one runner produced the report and the artifacts.
confirmed.evidence: Line 403: `state = actual.get('status', 'NOT_RUN')`. Line 409 compares only expected and source. Line 428 stores observed with no comparison. The CaseRunner runtime record carries expected/source/status but not op/unit/where/field/baseline (CaseRunner.java ~442-446), so these cannot be compared at all.
confirmed.fix: Have the assembler independently re-evaluate every PASS assertion over the captured action bytes, using the declared op/unit/where/field/baseline, and FAIL on any contradiction. Emit op and filters in runtime records and require them to equal the declared ones.

verdict.reasoning:
The mechanism is real, but the claim gets some details wrong and overstates the severity. It is a defense-in-depth gap, not a P2 weak oracle.

Confirmed by reading the code:
- `verification/coverage/assemble.py:403` copies the runner's assertion status: `state = actual.get('status', 'NOT_RUN')`.
- Line 409 compares only `expected` and `source` against the declared assertion.
- Lines 410-428 resolve the raw pointer values into `link['observed']`, but nothing compares them with `expected`.
- `test_coverage.py`, `validate.py` and `validate_saved` never re-evaluate either. `validate_saved` re-runs the same assembly, so it is not a second evaluator.
- Actual profiles are built by `./verify` with `-Dmaven.test.skip=true`. The coverage gate's PROFILES list has no `harness` profile, so no same-commit unit-test evidence for `AssertionEngine` is required.
- Conclusion: if `AssertionEngine` or `CaseRunner` regressed at the evaluated commit, the assembler would turn a contradicting PASS into an observation PASS. The scenario is reachable in principle.

What the claim gets wrong or overstates:
1. "Never compares filters" is false for the main source. In all 20,473 case assertions, `where` and `field` sit inside the `source` object (7,577 use them; none sit at the top level). Line 409 compares the whole `source` object, so main-source filters are compared. Only `baseline`, `unitSource`, `baselineUnitSource`, `op` and `unit` are not compared.
2. Comparing `op` would add almost nothing. `CaseRunner.assertId` (`CaseRunner.java:240`, not ~442-446; the file has 302 lines) copies `expected`, `source`, `requirementRefs` and `evidenceRefs` from the same case file, and `caseHash` already binds that file. Echo checks like this cannot catch an evaluator bug. Only re-evaluation would.
3. Plan §13.4 asks the coverage verifier to check that assertions and artifacts are actually linked, not to evaluate the oracles a second time. `verification/coverage/README.md` says this outright: assembly checks only integrity and links. It says semantic oracle equivalence needs case/runtime review and that the assembler issues no attestation. The manifest emits `semanticOracleEquivalence: REQUIRES_CASE_AND_RUNTIME_REVIEW`. So nothing claims this protection exists.
4. The failure needs a second, independent bug in the test oracle itself. `AssertionEngine` has unit tests, and `AssertionEngineTest.wrongQuantityFails` covers exactly this case: 100 expected, 80 observed, AssertionError.

Residual real gap:
- The PASS gate never requires those evaluator unit tests to have passed at the same commit.
- For where/field assertions, `observed` stores the raw unfiltered array rather than the filtered/projected value that was compared. This makes the manual review the README relies on harder.

Cheaper fixes than a full Python re-implementation:
- Require same-commit `./verify harness` / `AssertionEngineTest` evidence in coverage PASS.
- Have the runner emit the post-filter/projection compared value, and have the assembler check it against the raw captured bytes.

Severity: P3 hardening.

unverifiedP3.title: `./verify coverage` still exits 0 with status PREPARED, and the Java profile reports can never satisfy the assembler's PASS conditions
unverifiedP3.failure_scenario: CI or an agent that runs the plan's `./verify coverage` sees exit 0 while runtime is NOT_RUN, because the command runs Java Main.prepare and never assemble.py. Wiring alone will not fix this. For the actual driver, Main forces gateComplete=false (Main.java:59) and emits discoveredSubcases/selectedSubcases (line 53). The assembler requires gateComplete is True and discovered==started==completed (assemble.py:332), so no Java-produced profile report can ever be PASS. S1–S3 were marked COMPLETE using separate actual/sN receipts outside the coverage assembler.
unverifiedP3.evidence: verify:67 passes 'coverage' to Main. Main.java:35 routes coverage to prepare(). Main.java:53 and 59 set the report fields described above. assemble.py:332 checks for the other field names. The unwired entrypoint was deferred as a known Step2 limitation; the field mismatch was not recorded.
unverifiedP3.fix: Make `./verify coverage` run assemble.py and return its exit code. Align the Java report fields (discovered/started/completed, gateComplete only when complete) with the assembler, and add a producer→consumer regression test like the one used for the earlier PREPARED enum fix.

unverifiedP3.title: Foreign/mixed-language quota (>=10) is checked only via the `languages` tag, not the utterance text
unverifiedP3.failure_scenario: A corpus edit that replaces Italian/English utterances with Korean text while leaving `languages: ['it']` still reports foreignOrMixedCases=21 and corpusIntegrity VALID, so §13.3's 'minimum 10 Italian/English or mixed originals' can be weakened without detection. (Current corpus is genuine: 16 of the 21 tagged cases have Latin-script utterances; M23/M41/M49 etc. are 'mixed' only by SKU/DOC tokens.)
unverifiedP3.evidence: validate.py: `foreign += bool(set(langs) & {'it', 'en'})` and `require(foreign >= 10, ...)`; no check of utterance script. Script over corpus.json confirmed tags vs text.
unverifiedP3.fix: For each case tagged it/en require the first utterance to contain a Latin-script word run of >=3 letters outside fixed ID tokens (or a per-case `foreignSourceText` excerpt verified verbatim), and count only those toward the >=10 minimum; add a mutation test.
